judged_text: The old code fell back to bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar (a duplicated operand, almost certainly intended to fall back to the user's destinationCalendar); the new code drops the fallback arm entirely rather than fixing it to user.destinationCalendar. A pre-existing bug is silently removed along with its intended fallback semantics; reschedule-request emails/updates for bookings without a booking-level destinationCalendar now run with an empty array where the author evidently meant to fall back to the user's calendar — the fix changed the objective (bug cleanup) without flagging it for review.

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a (buggy) duplicated fallback (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`) to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, which indeed removes any possibility of falling back to a user-level destination calendar. Other updated call sites in the same diff commonly fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` / `booking.user?.destinationCalendar` (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`), so this inconsistency is a concrete review concern and a potentially unintended behavior change. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove that reschedule requests must/should use the user fallback or that the empty array causes a definite runtime failure in this path.
